title: Migrate intake plugin to contract v2
goal: Move plugins/agent/intake to the v2 stage contract: v2 JSON result on every exit path, rc ∈ {0,1}, router budgets in manifest, name-matched inputs, primary: true JSON output, valid_verdicts enforced, tests first.

steps.description: Write v2 contract tests first (TDD — must fail before implementation). Amend intake-test.sh to: (a) change all rc=2 assertions on intake_run paths to rc=1; (b) assert intake-result.json exists after every invocation (success, closed-issue refusal, failed-fetch, empty-goal, branch-refused) and carries result_contract:2, a declared verdict, a declared disposition, and a non-empty reason; (c) assert that each valid_verdict the manifest will declare (pass, fail) is driven by at least one test case; (d) add a grep-based assertion that plugin.sh contains no hardcoded artifact dir paths; (e) add a passing-run golden snapshot test that captures state/scope-manifest.md and state/intake.md content and asserts they are unchanged relative to a v1 baseline fixture. Confirm the new assertions fail before any implementation change (red step for the PR body).

Migrate manifest.yaml to v2. Changes: (1) add result_contract: 2 under provides:; (2) add config.router.timeout_s and config.router.max_turns (intake is a T1 agent — router budget per #1816, even though no LLM call today; template override still wins); (3) replace valid_verdicts: [] with [pass, fail]; (4) add a new output intake-result.json (type intake-result.json@1, format json, required: true, primary: true) before the existing scope_manifest entry; (5) remove primary: true from the scope_manifest output (it is not the verdict-bearing primary under v2); (6) add a comment under cleanup hook section recording that intake holds no live resources and therefore declares no cleanup hook (ADR-054 §7); (7) inputs: stays [] — intake reads from the GitHub API (external source), not a declared inter-stage artifact. The scope_manifest output entry retains required: true. Verify lint-verdict-classify covers pass and fail.

Migrate plugin.sh to v2. Changes: (1) add a _intake_write_result helper that atomically writes intake-result.json (result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason, data:{}) to the artifact_dir, mirroring teardown's inline pattern but extracted to avoid repetition across ~6 call sites; (2) resolve artifact_dir early in intake_run from dirname(state_file)/artifacts or ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (the closed-issue refusal path fires before state_dir is derived, so artifact_dir must be computed before that branch); (3) at every exit path in intake_run, call _intake_write_result with the appropriate verdict (pass/fail) and disposition (complete, unavailable, misconfigured, or broken) before returning — specifically: no-goal+no-issue → fail/misconfigured; closed/locked issue → fail/unavailable; failed fetch (#1804) → fail/unavailable; empty state_file → fail/broken; empty-after-sanitization → fail/broken; branch refused → fail/misconfigured; success → pass/complete; (4) change every `return 2` in intake_run to `return 1` (lib functions _intake_create_workspace_branch etc. keep their own codes; intake_run normalizes at each call site). Do not touch the lib functions in lib/branch-ops.sh, lib/branch-names.sh, lib/sanitize.sh, lib/issue-state.sh — their return codes are internal to the plugin and are not the engine-facing rc.

Run npm test and confirm green. The new tests from step-1 must now pass (green after implementation), including: result file on every path, rc=0/1 only, golden diff unchanged, grep assertion clean. If npm run lint also exercises lint-verdict-classify and lint-disposition-words, confirm those pass too. Record the red-step assertion and how it failed in the PR body (required by CLAUDE.md). No new files created beyond what test and manifest require.

notes: 1. INPUTS STAY []: Intake reads state/platforms.json directly (written by core/detect/platforms.sh before intake runs) — this is not a declared inter-stage artifact, it is a runtime side-channel. The acceptance criterion about no-constructed-artifact-paths applies to INPUT artifacts; the grep test should confirm no path like ${artifact_dir}/... appears as a consumer path in plugin.sh. The state_dir-relative writes (scope-manifest.md, intake.md) are OUTPUT paths that still appear in code and in the manifest — that is expected under the current engine (ADR-055 §1's full path-resolution via #1826 is not yet complete). 2. SCOPE_MANIFEST PRIMARY: The issue says 'If this plugin already declares one, say so and move on' about primary: true — the existing primary is scope-manifest.md (markdown), which cannot carry result_contract/verdict/disposition/reason. Under v2, the primary must be the JSON result file. A new intake-result.json output becomes primary and scope-manifest.md drops primary: true. 3. CLEANUP: Intake holds no live resources (no spawned process groups, no locks, no open handles beyond what atomic_write closes immediately). The hook is absent. ADR-054 §7 says 'if it has nothing to free, the hook is absent and that is recorded, not implied' — recorded by a manifest comment and a test assertion that the manifest declares no cleanup hook. 4. ROUTER BUDGET VALUES: Intake makes no LLM calls today (T1 tier, no route_to_model). The #1816 requirement is that router budgets are declared in the manifest so the template override can win. Reasonable defaults: timeout_s: 120 (generous for gh API calls), max_turns: 0 (no turns needed). 5. INTERRUPTION PATH: The issue lists 'interruption' as an exit path that must produce a v2 result. Intake installs no signal trap directly — interruption arrives as a SIGINT/SIGTERM killing the subshell. The DoD says 'interruption' but ADR-054's interruption path is the engine's own signal trap writing a broken disposition if no result was left. For a T0-style synchronous plugin like intake, the practical approach is ensuring every normal exit path writes the result — a genuine mid-flight kill will leave no result and the engine classifies it as broken per ADR-054 §4. The test drives the declared paths; the interruption path is addressed by the engine's existing broken-result fallback. 6. GOLDEN DIFF: The 'before/after golden diff on the stage's own output' means the state/scope-manifest.md and state/intake.md content must be identical between a v1 and v2 run on the same input. This can be captured as a fixture (the expected content of both files for a canonical ZBUILD_GOAL) asserted in the test. The intake-result.json is NEW (no v1 baseline), so it is not part of the diff. 7. TRIPLICATED SCOPE-MANIFEST: The issue says intake is the 'producer half of the triplicated scope-manifest.md declaration.' Under v2 intake declares that output once (already done in manifest). The 'build references it' part is a build manifest change that is OUT OF SCOPE for this issue — the issue says 'each plugin moves on its own' and the engine reads v1 and v2 side by side. 8. TESTS IN intake-branch-test.sh: All rc=2 assertions there test _intake_create_workspace_branch (a lib function), not intake_run. They do not need updating — lib functions may return any code; only the contract-facing intake_run is narrowed to {0,1}.
